figures.caption: Figure 1: Good PPL on PG-19 in (a) does not translate to high reasoning accuracy on LongBench-E (b). HMM resolves this mismatch via hierarchical memory, mitigating semantic aliasing. Note that the y-axis in (a) denotes the negative of PPL for visual consistency with (b), higher is better.

Figure 2: Overview of HMM. (a) Cognitive Inspiration: Multi-stage human memory involving sensory, working, and long-term memory. (b) Technical Pipeline: Through a trainable working memory network, HMM firstly maps pre-trained Mamba hidden states (ht) (resembling sensory memory) to high-level semantic representation as long-term memory via Semantic Encoding (red arrow, Sec. 5.1), then retrieves and broadcasts them back to late layers of the pretrained backbone via Semantic Retrieval (green arrow, Sec. 5.2) to enhance the capability for long-context reasoning.

Table 3: Benchmark results on LongBench-E tasks. We compare HMM against Vanilla Mamba and recent long-context Mamba variants across various task categories. For task name abbreviations, refer to Appendix H.
Figure 4: (a) Memory footprint comparison between Mamba2 and HMM across context lengths. (b) Sensitivity to segmentation hyperparameters (τ, p). (c) Layer-wise boundary detection performance.
